# Independent audit: atomic hinge descent and the nonregular tilted barycenter

Audit target:
`candidate f324bc23ceb65e89`.

regularity-free necessary barycenter condition for a joint UNPENALIZED
bad minimum. No penalty derivative is omitted: this note does not apply
the conclusion to a penalized objective.

## 1. Complete hinge theorem audit

Convexity of the actual buffered level region gives midpoint closure,
indeed lattice completeness, of the deepest-base set I. The maximal-
threshold argument uses closed bad caps and their complementary strict
inequalities. Every nonsaturated cap has an actual deepest equality
witness strict for all other inequalities. Their parities are distinct
by midpoint closure. The compressed caps remain subsets of old mass-Q
caps but contain witnesses of atomic depth Q, so their FULL-family
masses equal Q. This verifies both the count m<=k(I) and all boundary
atoms; the cover is not merely a geometric trace on I.

A tiny positive offset makes each hinge positive exactly on its selected
cap trace. Its surface-weighted normalizing cost D_i is finite and positive,
including H_0=2 in continuous dimension one. The sum h=sum h_i/D_i is
nonnegative convex in the base. For an actual anchored representation,
if X_j+t h(z_j) Ball lies in K_zj, then

    sum lambda_j X_j+t[sum lambda_j h(z_j)] Ball
                                      lies in K_z0.

Convexity gives h(z0)<=sum lambda_j h(z_j), proving EXACT compatibility
of every eroded target. This handles inputs outside a selected cap and
is precisely what a uniform closed-minor contraction did not preserve.
Positive old inradii ensure all eroded fibers stay positive. The bounded
radial first variation for constant inward speed gives total first loss
D=m and selected-cap loss at least one, with all overlaps paid positively.

Each old maximizing fiber has a fixed pure-base upper cap from this menu.
The remaining bases have a uniform strict gap and remain below the cover
under positive Hausdorff continuity. The actual updated energy, covariance,
M and geometric-mean affine multiplier are retained. Thus the printed
normalized upper derivative (beta m-D_Gi)/M is correct, and is negative
under beta<1/k(I). This is an actual local descent, not a merely formal
response inequality. No regular continuous sections are needed.

## 2. A strict fixed-body monotonicity lemma

Fix a compatible body, its M and Sigma, and epsilon>0. Let the positive
affine multiplier vary. At a fixed sampled base p its buffered source
depths depend on that multiplier only through its positive scalar value
ell(p). Write q_p(l) for the maximum over its actual fiber when that
value is l>0. Suppose

    0<q_p(l)<b_base(p).

Then for EVERY 0<l'<l,

    q_p(l')<q_p(l).                                         (1)

Proof. Reducing l reduces every positive interior buffer threshold radius,
so pointwise monotonicity gives q_p(l')<=q_p(l). Suppose equality held
and choose an attained maximizing mark y for l'. It would also be a
maximizer for l. Positive depth makes y interior: at an own boundary
point E=0, and a continuous supporting normal of K_p extends by the
finite support LP to a global affine support plane. Its closed mixed
cap has zero d-volume in every fiber, so the unbuffered and buffered
depths there are zero.

At this interior y there is an attained active nonvertical cap for l,
because its value is strictly below the atomic base depth. The fixed-
matrix tilt-compression argument supplies attainment. The whole-fiber
capture lemma implies this active cap has a proper own trace: any cap
containing all K_p has mixed mass at least b_base(p). Reducing l raises
its threshold strictly while keeping that threshold below u.y. The
removed own strip has positive d-volume, since the old section was proper
and y is interior. The other fibers can only lose captured mass. Hence
this same normal/tilt at l' has mass strictly below q_p(l), contradicting
the equality. This proves (1).

No derivative of cap volume, smoothness of other fibers, supporting-facet
allocation, or uniform C1 quantile assertion appears in this proof. On a
compact near-active set the existing proper-own-coarea argument gives a
quantitative local version, but qualitative strictness already suffices.

## 3. Necessary tilted barycenter at a joint unpenalized bad minimum

Assume an actual positive family and positive affine ell, geometrically
normalized by sum_z w_z log ell_z=0, jointly locally minimize the
UNPENALIZED normalized buffered maximum beta=Q/M. Suppose

    beta<1/k(P).

Let I be the deepest bases and set

    J={p in I: Q<b_base(p)},
    Z=sum_z w_z/ell_z,
    g_tilt=[sum_z w_z z/ell_z]/Z.                            (2)

Then

    J is nonempty and g_tilt belongs to conv(J).              (3)

If J were empty, the audited all-atomic hinge theorem would already give
a strict local descent, since k(I)<=k(P). So suppose J is nonempty and
g_tilt is outside its convex hull. Strict separation supplies an affine
function psi with

    psi(p)<0 for every p in J,      psi(g_tilt)=0.

Consequently sum_z w_z psi(z)/ell_z=Z psi(g_tilt)=0. Perturb the raw
affine multiplier to ell+t psi and rescale by its actual geometric mean,
keeping the body fixed. Positivity holds for small t. Its derivative is

    dot ell_z=psi(z)-ell_z sum_q w_q psi(q)/ell_q=psi(z).

Thus for every p in J its normalized value is strictly smaller for all
sufficiently small positive t. By (1) the WHOLE base maximum at every
such p becomes strictly smaller than Q. This does not assume that old
maximizers remain the relevant marks.

For old atomic bases p in I outside J, the unchanged pure-base depth
bounds every new marked point by Q. All bases outside I stay strictly
below Q by the finite old gap and fixed-body parameter continuity. Hence
the new global maximum Q_t is at most Q. If it is smaller, the parameter
variation itself is a strict descent. Otherwise EVERY new deepest base
belongs to the old atomic set, and has unchanged atomic depth Q.

Apply the all-atomic hinge theorem at this new positive pair. Its level
is still beta<1/k(P)<=1/k(I_t), so it admits an arbitrarily small actual
strict body descent. Take the initial parameter perturbation and this
second path small enough to remain inside the original local-minimum
neighborhood. Their composition contradicts local minimality. This
proves (3), with no regular cap or singleton-contact premise.

The two-stage argument uses an EXACT weak bound Q_t<=Q followed by an
actual strict descent. It is not a forbidden derivative subtraction or
a formal neutral-path continuation. The multiplier and covariance in the
second step are updated as in the hinge theorem.

## 4. Geometry of the proper-gap deepest stratum

The set J in (2) is itself lattice-complete. If it is nonempty, finiteness
provides a positive gap

    eta=min_(p in J)[b_base(p)-Q]>0.

The atomic base-depth superlevel {b_base>=Q+eta} is convex in the usual
real-base depth-region sense. The buffered Q-superlevel is also convex.
For any lattice point in conv(J), interpolate actual deepest marks:
compatibility and buffered convexity make its mark deepest, while atomic
convexity makes its base depth at least Q+eta. Thus it belongs to J.
Since conv(J) lies in conv(P), there are no additional lattice sites,
proving J=conv(J) intersect Lambda.

All weights w_z/ell_z in (2) are strictly positive. Therefore g_tilt lies
in the relative interior of conv(P). By (3), conv(J) meets that relative
interior; in particular J is not contained in any proper exposed face.

These are necessary structural consequences. They do not prove that all
deepest bases are proper-gap, remove atomic groups from a moving global
cover, supply a universal numerical payment, or justify discarding a
penalty term. Those separate obligations are retained.
